pattern.crimePattern: a client who blames a mountain guide for her brother's altitude death kills her near the summit and forges her signature in the park exit register
pattern.notes: Fictional guide, client, porter and rangers. Altitude deaths and guides' grief are treated with care; the inquiry found the guide blameless and the case never suggests otherwise. Route details are simplified for the cultural reader to check.

ob.text: KWS rangers at the Naro Moru gate report a mountain guide, Nkatha Mutuma (33), missing. Her clients checked out on Wednesday. The exit register shows she signed out with them.

evidence.title: Comparison view: exit vs entry signature

facts.text: Nkatha Mutuma, mountain guide, is reported missing. Her clients checked out on Wednesday; the exit register shows her signing out with them.
Exit register, Wednesday 16:20: W. Mwandawiro, M. Nderi, and "N. Mutuma" in the guide's column.
Register, Sunday entry page: Nkatha's signature is a quick looped "Nkatha M."
Nkatha's guide licence: her specimen signature, looped, matching the entry.
Josphine: "Three came in. At checkout I was dealing with a bus of students. The woman signed the book for the group. I didn't see the guide's face."
Josphine was on duty at the gate all week.
Josphine: the trip's declared kit was poles and crampons; no ice axe.
Josphine: Mwirigi Thiongo lost three regular clients to Nkatha this year and "said things".
Josphine: Nkatha's boyfriend, Muriungi, phoned the gate twice on Thursday asking where she was.
Josphine: the porter's fee was paid in full at checkout, on the trip voucher.
Mackinder's hut log: Wakio and Nkatha out for the summit at 02:30 on Wednesday; Murimi stayed with a sore knee. Wakio back at 08:40, alone.
The hut keeper: Murimi was in the porters' room all that morning.
KWS incident report: three years ago Baraka Mwandawiro, 22, died of high-altitude cerebral oedema; guide Nkatha Mutuma; no fault, he hid his symptoms.
Records, Wakio's line: no signal on the mountain; on Wednesday at 17:05, at the gate, KSh 20,000 to Murimi Nderi.
Murimi's receipt: KSh 20,000 from Wakio Mwandawiro, Wednesday 17:05.
Nkatha lay 120 m below the ridge path; her own two poles strapped to her pack, intact.
Beside her in the rocks: the broken carbide tip of a trekking pole, not from hers.
Her purse is in her pack with KSh 6,000.
Hotel registration card, room 14, in Wakio's own hand; a flight from Nanyuki airstrip on Saturday at 14:00.
Wakio's left trekking pole is missing its tip.
Shipton's Camp hut log: Mwirigi guiding on the Sirimon route all week, at Shipton's on Wednesday.
Meru roster: Muriungi at work in Meru, Sunday to Wednesday.
Post-mortem: two blows to the head from a narrow, pointed object before the fall; the fall injuries came after.
Post-mortem: death on Wednesday morning, between 05:30 and 07:30.
Post-mortem: no altitude oedema, no hypothermia; she died the same morning.
Comparison view: the entry signature traced on tracing paper and slid over "N. Mutuma". Careful, printed, slanting the other way. The loops refuse to line up.
A park register has no stamp or seal at all; every line is ballpoint ink.
A park register has no witness column, no index number and no parcel numbers: name, ID, role, time.
The exit line is dated Wednesday, three days after the Sunday entry.
Lab: the carbide tip fits Wakio's broken left pole exactly.
Wilfrida Ayugi: the exit "N. Mutuma", Wakio's own exit signature and her hotel card. "Same hand wrote all three."
Wakio: "Nkatha came down with us and signed out. She said she was going to see friends in Naro Moru."
Wakio: "I'd never met her before this climb."
Wakio: Nkatha "walked my brother up a mountain until his brain swelled". On the ridge at dawn, alone with her, "I asked her one question."
Wakio: "I never raised my pole to her. She slipped."
Murimi: "I saw Nkatha at the gate. She left with us."
Murimi: Madam said Nkatha had gone ahead with another group and paid him to say she came down. "Madam came down from the ridge alone. Look below the summit path."
Mwirigi: "I hated losing clients to her. I was on Sirimon."
Muriungi: "We fought about her being away so much. I was at work."

interrogations.intro: Wakio sits by her hotel window with the mountain behind her. "Nkatha came down with us and signed out. She said she was going to see friends in Naro Moru. I'd never met her before this climb."
Murimi rubs his strapped knee and won't look up. "I saw Nkatha at the gate. She left with us."
Mwirigi answers on the radio from Shipton's Camp, wind in the handset. "I hated losing clients to her. I was on Sirimon."
Muriungi has driven from Meru and hasn't slept. "We fought about her being away so much. I was at work."
Josphine turns the register round on the counter. "Three came in. I remember that."

contradictions.reaction: "Madam said Nkatha went ahead with another group. She paid me to say she came down. I needed the money. The guide's body is up there? On the ridge below the summit path, then. Madam came down from the ridge alone."
Wakio turns from the window. "She killed my brother. She walked him up a mountain until his brain swelled. I asked her one question at the top."
She looks at the incident report, her brother's name typed in it, and her mouth goes tight.
Wakio looks at the tip in its evidence bag. "He begged her not to turn back," she says. "She told me that. As if it helped."

reconstruction.text: Three years ago Wakio's brother Baraka dies of altitude sickness below Point Lenana. His guide is Nkatha. The inquiry finds no fault: he hid his symptoms. Wakio never accepts it, and books Nkatha by name.
Wednesday, 02:30. Wakio and Nkatha leave Mackinder's for the summit. Murimi stays behind with his knee.
At dawn on the ridge, alone, Wakio asks about Baraka. Nkatha tells her the truth: he begged her not to turn back. Wakio strikes her twice with her trekking pole and pushes her down the scree.
08:40. Wakio is back at the hut alone: "She went ahead to check on another group." At the gate at 16:20, while the ranger deals with a bus of students, she signs the guide's column herself.
17:05. KSh 20,000 to Murimi, to say Nkatha came down with them. Her flight leaves Nanyuki airstrip on Saturday.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Wakio and a warrant on her hotel room. The mountain costs time: the search team needs 8 hours to reach the scree. Wakio flies on Saturday at 14:00, so detain her once the warrant finds the broken pole; the tool marks (8 h) and handwriting (10 h) come back inside 24 hours. No rush needed.
